blocks.text: Virtual machines let many isolated workloads share one physical server, turning hardware into a pool that could be sliced, moved, copied and restored in software.

rows: Much higher utilization; fewer servers, less power
One VM's crash or compromise rarely affects others
Windows and Linux on one host
VM disk and state as files

items: Strongest general-purpose isolation for multi-tenant workloads.
Different kernels and OSes on one host.
Cloud instances are VMs; most containers in production run inside VMs.
MicroVMs (Firecracker, Kata Containers) bring VM isolation to container-style workloads.

blocks.text: Q: "Why do cloud providers still run containers inside VMs?" A: "VMs provide a hardware-enforced isolation boundary between tenants, each with its own kernel, while containers share one kernel. Providers use VMs (or microVMs like Firecracker) for tenant isolation, and containers inside them for packaging and density."

items: VMs made hardware poolable and software-defined.
Isolation is at the hypervisor, with separate kernels.
Snapshots and live migration changed operations.
VMs remain the isolation layer beneath containers.
